summary: A photo-essay style note surveying folk festivals around the world from September to December 2023, each tied to a photographer who documented it. It covers St. Martin's Eve in Ledbury, the Cornucopia Festival in Parma, the Viennese Autumn Ball, Saint Eloi in Provence, Diwali in Leicester, the Montreal Snow Festival and Inti Raymi in Cusco. The note stresses how each festival preserves history, belief and community tradition.
one_line: Photo-essay tour of seven folk festivals worldwide, from Ledbury to Cusco, in autumn and winter 2023, highlighting their traditions and photographers.
key_facts: St. Martin's Eve in Ledbury, England, took place on September 5, 2023, commemorating the town's patron saint, Martin of Tours.
Photographer Eliza Hampstead documented Ledbury's lantern procession led by children and dancers in medieval attire reenacting scenes from St. Martin's life.
St. Martin is remembered for splitting his cloak to share with a beggar, an act emulated by the town's generosity.
Parma, Italy, hosts the Cornucopia Festival in mid-September to mark the end of the harvest season; the Parade of Abundance is held on September 18.
The Parade of Abundance in Parma features folktale characters such as the Corn Maiden and Bacchus on floats decorated with produce; Layla Rossi photographed it.
The Viennese Autumn Ball was held on October 2, 2023, at the Hofburg of Vienna, with Strauss's "Blue Danube" and photography by Johann Becker.
The festival of Saint Eloi, patron saint of metalworkers and farriers, is held on November 25th in Provence, France, with hammer-on-anvil blessings; Renaud Giroux photographed it.
Diwali in Leicester was celebrated on November 14, 2023, with fireworks over the Golden Mile; Diwali is called the "Festival of Lights" and signifies the victory of light over darkness.
Amit Patel photographed Leicester's Diwali, including children with sparklers, oil lamps, saris, sweets and prayer ceremonies.
The Montreal Snow Festival began on December 1, 2023, with snow sculptures, ice skating, snowball fights and hot cocoa; Anne-Sophie Tremblay photographed it.
Inti Raymi, the Inca Festival of the Sun, was celebrated on December 22, 2023, in Cusco, Peru, reenacting homage to the sun god Inti.
Inti Raymi is staged at the plains of Sacsayhuaman, where thousands gather; Carlos Nuñez photographed participants in Incan tunics and headdresses.
